rules.title: Service executable can be overwritten
rules.subject: {name}
rules.why: Anyone who can overwrite a service's executable gets their code run under the service's account (usually LocalSystem) the next time the service starts or the machine reboots.
rules.fix: Remove write, modify and full-control entries for non-admin accounts from the executable, e.g. icacls "<executable>" /remove:g "BUILTIN\Users" (use the account named in the evidence). Service binaries should be writable only by SYSTEM, Administrators and TrustedInstaller. If an installer set these rights, a reinstall will put them back, so report it to the vendor too.

rules.title: Service folder lets non-admins add files
rules.subject: {name}
rules.why: Windows looks in a program's own folder first when it loads a DLL. A DLL dropped into this folder under the name of one the service loads runs under the service's account.
rules.fix: Remove 'create files / write data' rights for non-admin accounts on the folder (icacls "<folder>" /remove:g <account>). Programs installed outside Program Files (e.g. C:\Tools\...) inherit Authenticated Users: Modify from C:\, so install services under Program Files instead.

rules.title: Unquoted service path can be hijacked
rules.subject: {name}
rules.why: The service's path has spaces and no quotes, so Windows first tries each space-separated prefix as a program (C:\Program.exe, C:\Program Files\Some.exe, ...). One of those locations is writable, so a program placed there runs under the service's account.
rules.fix: Quote the path in HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\<service>\ImagePath, e.g. "C:\Program Files\Some App\app.exe" -args, or with sc config <service> binPath= ... Also remove write access from the folder named in the evidence.

rules.title: Unquoted service path contains spaces
rules.subject: {name}
rules.why: Not exploitable as things stand: none of the folders Windows would try first is writable. It becomes exploitable as soon as one of them is.
rules.fix: Quote the path in HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\<service>\ImagePath, e.g. "C:\Program Files\Some App\app.exe" -args.

rules.title: Service executable is missing and non-admins can create it
rules.subject: {name}
rules.why: The service points at a program that no longer exists, in a place where non-admins can create it. Whoever puts a program there gets it run under the service's account (usually LocalSystem) the next time the service starts.
rules.fix: If the software was uninstalled, delete the leftover service from an elevated prompt (sc delete <service>). Otherwise reinstall it, or create the folder with an ACL that only lets SYSTEM and Administrators write to it.
